- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (e.g., < 0.5 or 0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast slope or adding downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >90), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply lagged mean reversion or cap forecast at +5–10% above recent peak.
- In periods of high sentiment (e.g., >0.7), model underestimates volatility; increase forecast volatility or add upward bias to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a forecast peak, model fails to adjust; trigger downward correction rule with sensitivity to sentiment decay.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overfits recent trends; apply smoothing or decay factor to reduce influence of last 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.00–0.3), model tends to drift toward historical mean; use mean reversion heuristic with 10–15% buffer to avoid underprediction.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after forecast peak, model is too optimistic; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods.
